\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Two Point Calculus}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Sharp.TwoPointCalculus
\section{Overview}
Convexity of symmetric power expressions yields supporting-line inequalities adapted to a biased two-point law. These estimates give the normalized and general nonnegative two-point bounds.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Slope comparison for symmetric powers]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.symmetric_power_slope_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $1<p<2$ and $0\le t<1$. Then $(1+t)^{p-1}-(1-t)^{p-1}\le(p-1)t((1+t)^{p-2}+(1-t)^{p-2})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Convexity of symmetric square-root powers]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.convexOn_symmetric_sqrt_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.symmetric_power_slope_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $1<p<2$. The function $z\mapsto(1+\sqrt z)^p+(1-\sqrt z)^p$ is convex on $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Convexity of a biased power expression]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.convexOn_biased_power}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.convexOn_symmetric_sqrt_rpow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $1<p<2$. The function $z\mapsto((1+\sqrt z)^p+(1-\sqrt z)^p)^{2/p}$ is convex on $[0,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Supporting line for the biased power expression]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.biased_power_tangent_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.convexOn_biased_power}
\difficulty{5}
Let $1<p<2$, $0<t<1$, and $0\le z\le1$. Put $S=(1+t)^p+(1-t)^p$. Then $S^{2/p}+S^{2/p-1}\frac{(1+t)^{p-1}-(1-t)^{p-1}}t(z-t^2)\le((1+\sqrt z)^p+(1-\sqrt z)^p)^{2/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Supporting-line coefficients at the bias]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.tangent_at_bias}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $1<p<2$, $0<\alpha<\beta$, and $\alpha^p+\beta^p=1$. Put $t=(\beta-\alpha)/(\beta+\alpha)$ and $S=(1+t)^p+(1-t)^p$. Then $S^{2/p}=4/(\alpha+\beta)^2$ and $S^{2/p-1}((1+t)^{p-1}-(1-t)^{p-1})/t=2(\beta^{p-1}-\alpha^{p-1})/(\beta-\alpha)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Normalized biased quadratic inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.normalized_biased_quadratic_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.biased_power_tangent_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.tangent_at_bias}
\difficulty{6}
Let $1<p<2$, $0<\alpha<\beta$, $\alpha^p+\beta^p=1$, and $-1\le y\le1$. Put $r=(\alpha^p\beta^{2-p}-\alpha^{2-p}\beta^p)/(\alpha^2-\beta^2)$. Setting $u=(1+y)/\alpha$ and $v=(1-y)/\beta$, one has $(\alpha^pu+\beta^pv)^2+r\alpha^p\beta^p(u-v)^2\le((1+y)^p+(1-y)^p)^{2/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative biased two-point inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.nonnegative_biased_two_point_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.normalized_biased_quadratic_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $1<p<2$, $0<\alpha<\beta$, $\alpha^p+\beta^p=1$, and $u,v\ge0$. Put $r=(\alpha^p\beta^{2-p}-\alpha^{2-p}\beta^p)/(\alpha^2-\beta^2)$. Then $(\alpha^pu+\beta^pv)^2+r\alpha^p\beta^p(u-v)^2\le(\alpha^pu^p+\beta^pv^p)^{2/p}$.
\end{theorem}
